html:
The Contract of the Century was a deal signed in Baku on 20 September 1994 with a group of foreign oil firms led by BP to develop three large oil fields under the Caspian Sea. Azerbaijan's state oil company was the partner.

It was the first big Western investment in the former Soviet south. Oil began to flow in 1997, and the Baku Tbilisi Ceyhan pipeline, opened in 2006, carried it to the Mediterranean through Georgia and Turkey, avoiding Russia. Oil money transformed Baku with towers and boulevards and paid for the army that won the war of 2020. It also tied Azerbaijan's economy almost entirely to oil and gas.
